**Updated by:** Builder — **the identity ruling implemented (Chris, 2026-08-05): FieldScout stores no name for a person**, branch `fix/identity-username-only-v2`. Not a milestone task — a whole-app ruling that lands across the league surface, so it is recorded here. Chris, verbatim: *"we don't need either a display name or a full name. we just need the email, password and unique username."* `handle_new_user` seeded `profiles.display_name` from the OAuth `full_name` claim, so a Google sign-in wrote a REAL NAME into a row that the `profiles` policy "Profiles are viewable by everyone" USING (true) exposes to **anon** — and every identity surface rendered `display_name ?? @username` (Chris saw his own name across the app). **Migration 075** does two things and no more: `handle_new_user`'s profile INSERT becomes `(id, username, avatar_url)` — no name written, the OAuth claim ignored — and `UPDATE profiles SET display_name = NULL` clears the names already stored. **No schema change**: the column is NULLABLE with no default, so once nothing writes it it sits inert, and the migration and the app deploy are order-independent against the live site (this is what sank the earlier PR #96, which renamed the column to `full_name` and called it private — the world-readable policy made that untrue, and neither merge order was safe). The migration body is production's LIVE `handle_new_user` (`pg_get_functiondef`, 2026-08-05) minus the name write — it deliberately does NOT import the 049/050/051 username-contract guards, which were never applied to production and which 073 reverted locally too; restoring them is a real but SEPARATE bug, flagged not smuggled (see D115(3)). The five other functions that read the column (`notify_list_followers`, `create_league`, `seat_league_member_internal`, `get_join_preview`, `draft_actor_name`) are deliberately NOT replaced: each reads through a `COALESCE` onto `username`, so with the column permanently NULL they already resolve to the handle — zero churn, and three of them do not exist in production at all. `ai_personas.display_name` is untouched (PUBLIC parody brand copy carrying the "(AI)" transparency marker — no human behind it, nothing to leak; PR #96's `persona_name` rename is dropped). Spec **v2.9** folds the ruling into §7.2's identity table + render rule, §7.2.1's retained-history line, §12.23's claim-preview comment and §16.4's growth-loop rule. Account settings loses its name field entirely: email, password, avatar and a read-only permanent handle. New vitest `src/lib/identity-render.test.ts` (10): source-level sweep of every surface (the `launch-scope-gates` precedent) — no code reads or writes a name on a profile, no PostgREST select pulls one out of `profiles`, settings offers no name field, no seed/dev script plants one, and 075 makes no `ALTER TABLE`/`RENAME`/`DROP COLUMN` at all. pgTAP 005's R31 slot now asserts the trigger writes **no** name (the strongest form of that guard). **Search narrowed to handle-only matching** — there is nothing else left to match on. D115. ## 3. Spec questions

*Anything where the spec is ambiguous, silent, or seems wrong. Write it here and STOP rather than improvising — per CLAUDE.md. Move to "Resolved" once Chris answers; the answer should also get folded back into the spec itself as a changelog entry.*

### Open

**None currently.** *(The draft-room redesign's three questions — **Q12** chrome-free scope · **Q13** Exit Draft · **Q14** the two-tabs guard — were all **RULED by Chris 2026-08-17** and folded into the spec the same day; see Resolved below. No DR task was ever gated on them.)*

### Resolved

**Q14 — The two-tabs guard: hard takeover, or two live tabs? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §9.3's v2.12 note + tasks-DR D156. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.6 builds the recommendation and a reversal is a small change.)**

**Evidence.** Chris ruled that in-app desktop entry opens the room in a **new browser tab** (§16.1). A user can therefore trivially hold two tabs of one draft — and nothing today notices. Each tab opens its own socket and its own `draft:<id>` subscription (`use-draft.ts:244` — the only `.channel(` call in `src/`), runs its own 15s `draft_touch` liveness heartbeat (`use-draft.ts:394–413`), and tracks presence under the same key (presence is keyed by team id), so the room's presence list shows one manager twice. §9.3's budget is written per *client* — "one socket per client, ≤ 3 channels" — and says nothing about one user holding several. **Correctness is not at risk** (the server is authoritative per §8.1, so a stale tab's action is refused by the ordinary validators); what is at risk is fan-out, quota, and a presence list that lies.

**Options:**
- **(a) Hard takeover — newest tab wins (recommended).** The newest tab of a draft holds the connection; older tabs unsubscribe, stop the heartbeat, and show a plain "This draft is open in another tab" state with a **"Use this tab instead"** button. Client-local coordination (`BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id, `localStorage` fallback), scoped **per browser profile** so a laptop and a phone are untouched. One live room per browser: presence is honest, fan-out is bounded, and the failure mode is a screen that tells you exactly what happened and how to fix it.
- **(b) Both tabs stay live; dedupe presence only.** Nothing is taken away from the user, but the fan-out doubling stays, the heartbeats double, and the presence dedupe has to be right or the list is wrong anyway — most of the work of (a) for less of the benefit.
- **(c) Do nothing.** Defensible on correctness grounds alone, and wrong on draft night: a manager with two tabs open sees themselves twice in the room and does not know which tab is real.

**Recommendation: (a).** It is the option that makes the presence list true, and the takeover button means a user who lands on the stale tab is never stuck. Flagged for you because it is a visible behavior — one of your tabs going quiet is something you would want to have chosen.

**What's gated:** nothing. DR.6 builds (a) unless you say otherwise.

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a) — hard takeover, newest tab wins.** Verbatim: *"The most recent one takes over and the others disconnect."* Build exactly as recommended: the **newest tab of a given draft holds the connection**; older tabs **unsubscribe the `draft:<id>` channel and stop the `draft_touch` heartbeat**, then render the plain "This draft is open in another tab" state with a **Use this tab instead** button that takes the connection back. Coordination is a `BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id with a `localStorage` fallback, scoped **per browser profile** — a laptop and a phone remain two legitimate live clients and are untouched. Nothing about the mechanics changes from the recommendation, so the spec text folded at v2.12 stands as written and is now a **ruling rather than a working assumption** (§9.3's two-tabs guard, marked in place). **DR.6 builds it** (tasks-DR §5; D156).

---

**Q13 — Exit Draft: where does it go, and should leaving mid-draft warn? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §16.4 zone 1. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.2 builds the recommendation.)**

**Evidence.** You ruled **Exit Draft appears in the top bar for both commissioner and non-commissioner** — everyone must be able to leave. With the room in its own browser tab (desktop), "leaving" has two plausible meanings that the shipped **Exit room** link (`snake-draft-room.tsx:704–706`, a plain link to `/app/leagues/[id]`) never had to distinguish: navigate this tab back to the league, or close the tab. There is a hard constraint on the second: **`window.close()` only works on a tab a script opened**, so it would work when you came from the in-app CTA and **fail silently** on a deep link, a refresh, or a bookmarked room — the worst kind of button.

**Options:**
- **(a) Navigate in place to league home; never close the tab; no confirmation (recommended).** One behavior on every entry path, no silent failures. No warning on the way out because leaving costs nothing real — the draft continues without you and autopick covers your picks (§8.4), which is exactly what it is for.
- **(b) Navigate in place, but confirm when it is YOUR turn.** Honest about the one moment leaving is expensive. Costs a modal on the room's most time-pressured surface, and the clock keeps running while you read it.
- **(c) Try to close the tab, fall back to navigating.** Rejected: the same button does two different things depending on how you arrived, and users learn buttons by what they did last time.

**Recommendation: (a)**, with (b) available later as a small addition if test-cohort feedback says people leave by accident. Flagged because "Exit" doing something you did not expect is a trust problem, not a polish problem.

**What's gated:** nothing. DR.2 builds (a).

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a)'s MECHANICS — navigate in place to league home, never `window.close()`, no confirmation — but the REASON is different from the one recommended, and the reason is what gets built.** Verbatim: *"Exit draft just exits you from the draft room and after a certain amount of time puts you into 'auto draft' mode. Which is how all mock drafts work."*

**The recommendation's rationale is corrected here.** It said "no warning because leaving costs nothing real". That is wrong: **leaving DOES hand your picks to the engine — and that is intended and expected**, the incumbent mental model Chris is naming (you leave, the bots draft for you). The mechanics are unchanged; what changes is that the behavior is a *stated feature*, not a cost to be papered over.

**Which mechanism — the load-bearing half of this ruling.** Two distinct autopick paths exist and **Exit triggers only the first**:
- **The D102 away path (§8.5.5's v2.8.13 erratum, migration 068) — THIS is what Exit fires.** The room's `draft_touch` heartbeat stops when you leave; after the 45s freshness constant (`draft_liveness_freshness()`, `068_draft_tick_autopick.sql:347–355` — 3 × the 15s room cadence) the seat reads **STALE**; at each of that manager's deadlines the pick is then **held open for `disconnect_grace_seconds`** (§7.3.8, default 30) and autopicked from queue → primary board → Big Board → ADP (§8.4). **Returning to the room restores manual control immediately** — the next heartbeat re-freshens the seat, and a manager who returns mid-hold may still pick by hand (E3).
- **The persistent `is_autodraft` toggle** (`league_members.is_autodraft`, §8.4's "Auto-draft me"; §12.2:762). This keeps autopicking **even after you come back**, until it is explicitly switched off.

**Exit must trigger the first and must NOT write the second.** `is_autodraft` is a deliberate, sticky choice a manager (or a commissioner on their behalf) makes; setting it on exit would silently strip a returning manager of manual control and make them hunt for a toggle to get it back. The heartbeat/staleness machinery already delivers exactly what Chris described, with the strictly better return-to-control property. **DR.2 must not touch `is_autodraft`**, and needs no new mechanism at all — Exit is a navigation.

**Verified against the code 2026-08-17 (the ruling depended on it, so it was checked rather than assumed).** The heartbeat is a `useEffect` at `src/hooks/use-draft.ts:394–413`; its cleanup (`:409–412`) calls `clearInterval(id)` and removes the `visibilitychange` listener. Navigating away unmounts the room, React runs that cleanup, and **no further `draft_touch` calls are made** — so leaving genuinely stops the heartbeat today. (The effect is additionally gated on `heartbeatActive` — defined at `:393`, early-returned at `:395` — so it never runs outside `live`/`paused`; and closing the tab stops the interval with or without the cleanup.) **There is no gap to close — DR.2 inherits working machinery** rather than owning a fix.

**Consequence for copy (part of the ruling, not a nicety).** Exit's affordance must say what actually happens. "Exit Draft" alone is not sufficient: the control states that **picks will be made from the manager's Targets while they are away, and that returning restores manual control**. The vehicle is the Builder's within the no-confirmation ruling — a `title`/tooltip on the control, a short line in the command bar, or a brief toast on the way out — but a confirmation modal is explicitly not one of the options (§16.5.4's designed-copy rule). Folded into spec §16.4 zone 1; **DR.2 owns it**.

**Q12 — Does the chrome-free full-screen treatment extend to the LOBBY and the RECAP? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §16.1's v2.12 note. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.1/DR.7 build the recommendation.)**

**Evidence.** Your ruling names "the Draft Room". Two neighbouring surfaces are not obviously in or out. **The lobby is not a choice:** it shares the `/draft` route and the room flips lobby→live **in place** (D120), so it inherits the chrome-free frame by construction — the only alternative would be splitting the route, which would break the in-place flip that makes draft-night feel live. **The recap is a real choice:** `…/draft/recap` (`src/app/app/leagues/[leagueId]/draft/recap/page.tsx`) is a separate route serving both the real and mock variants — a post-draft *reading* surface people revisit days later, where the nav, search and the right rail are useful rather than noise.

**Options:**
- **(a) Lobby chrome-free (forced), recap stays in the app shell (recommended).** The chrome-free treatment is for the live, time-pressured experience; the recap is a document. Keeping the recap in the shell also means the way *out* of it is the app's own nav rather than a bespoke exit.
- **(b) Both chrome-free.** Consistent — "everything under `/draft` is full-screen" is an easy rule to remember — but it puts a reading surface in a frame with no navigation, so every route out has to be rebuilt inside it.
- **(c) Lobby in the shell, room chrome-free.** Rejected on the mechanics above: it would break the in-place lobby→live flip.

**Recommendation: (a).** Recorded in spec v2.12 as the working assumption so the DR tasks have something to build; say the word and (b) is a small change to one route group.

**What's gated:** nothing.

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a) — the lobby and the live room are chrome-free; the recap keeps the app shell.** Verbatim: *"having a bunch unnecessary UI mid draft doesn't make sense… you need all the space you have for the draft surfaces"*, naming ESPN, Yahoo and Sleeper as doing exactly this.

**The framing above is replaced — Chris pushed back on it and he was right.** The full-screen treatment exists for **one reason: the live draft is space-hungry, and any app chrome on screen mid-draft is space taken from a draft surface.** That is a UX reason and it is the whole reason — not a route-mechanics argument, and not an open architectural question about where the app shell belongs. The lobby and the live room share the `/draft` route and are both part of that live surface, so both are chrome-free. **The recap was never in scope of the ruling**: it is not a draft surface at all — it is a post-draft reading page people revisit days later — so it keeps the app shell, and the app's own navigation is the way out of it.

Recorded as **a rule with its reason** in spec §16.1 (the v2.12 note's last paragraph rewritten in place) and in the **DR.1** / **DR.7** banners. *(If consistency is ever wanted, flipping the recap to full-screen is a one-route-group change — it moves from `(shell)` to `(room)` and nothing else changes.)*

**Q12 — §7.3.3.1 (spec v2.11, custom scoring editor): are K and D/ST editable in the test-cohort editor? (filed 2026-08-16 by the scoring-editor Architect session, PR #152.)** Chris's C37 requirements define the five sections for "every position except K and DEF" and named no K/D-ST sample players — silent on whether those two positions are editable at all. Options were **(a)** editable, one single-section page each; **(b)** template-locked (K/D-ST silently inherit the starting template's tables); **(c)** hidden entirely. Recommendation was (a).

**RULED 2026-08-16 (Chris): (a) — K and D/ST ARE editable**, one single-section page each, and the **sample players are NAMED, not generic: Neil Rackers (K) and the Seahawks (D/ST)**, joining Marino (QB) / Peterson (RB) / Moss (WR) / Gronk (TE). Their stat lines are written into §7.3.3.1 like the offensive four (K: 2 FG 0–39, 1 FG 40–49, 1 FG 50+, 3 PAT, 1 miss · D/ST: 3 sacks, 1 INT, 1 fumble rec, 1 def TD, 17 PA, 289 YA — the PA/YA figures deliberately sit near a family cut point so tier behavior is visible).

**CORRECTION recorded with the ruling (the filed question's option (a) was wrong on the facts and Chris pushed back):** the phrase *"the PA/YA bucketization chosen as a preset set (shared vs ESPN)"* implied points-allowed and yards-allowed are alternatives a commissioner picks between. **They are not.** They are two independent tables that pay **additively** — a defense's week is its events **plus** its PA tier **plus** (where the model carries one) its YA tier; ESPN pays both, the single-model platforms pay PA only (the D44 `dst_model` distinction). What actually varies between families is **where the tiers are cut** (ESPN 14–17/18–27/35–45/46+ vs shared 14–20/21–27/35+). Every site carrying the bad framing was rewritten in the same fold (§7.3.3.1 editable-scope + section catalog + guardrail 2, §23.5).

**RULED the same session — defense tiers, two parts.** **(a) The document format reserves per-league tier boundaries NOW** (`tier_cuts`), even though the UI ships later: cut points can only live in the league's own scoring doc, so adding them later would force a **third** format version plus a migration of every stored doc and a re-proof that every frozen draft snapshot still scores identically — deciding now costs nothing, deciding later costs a migration. Tier keys are **generated** from the cut list; the generation rule was **verified to regenerate all three of today's families byte-exactly** against `templates.ts` (ESPN PA 8 keys, shared PA 7, YA 9), which is the backward-compatibility argument and gets a pin. **(b) First-version UI inherits boundaries from the starting template and does NOT edit them** — no preset-set dropdown, no boundary fields; the commissioner edits **what each tier pays**. Boundary editing is its own task immediately after the editor: **ledger row F59**, routed to a follow-up Architect breakdown, explicitly not in the cohort editor build.

**RULED the same session — the boundary INPUT DESIGN, recorded now so the F59 follow-up inherits it:** boundaries are entered as **CUT POINTS, not ranges** — one ascending integer list per table (e.g. `0, 7, 14, 18, 28, 35, 46`), each tier derived as `[this cut, next cut)` with the last open-ended. This makes overlapping tiers and coverage gaps **structurally unconstructible** rather than validation-caught (freehand ranges admit both the F21 double-pay overlap and silent-zero gaps; derived-from-cuts admits neither — the same posture as the F21 guardrails). Residual validation is trivial: ascending, integers, ≥ 2 cuts; the PA and YA tables are independent (different domains, own cut lists).

**Q13 — §7.3.3.1/§23.5 (spec v2.11): `return_yards` for the Special Teams section — the stat does not exist in the system (no registry key, no `player_stats` column, no provider mapping). (filed 2026-08-16, PR #152.)** Chris's requirement (3) names Special Teams "e.g. return yards"; the only scorable special-teams key today is `return_td`. Options were **(a)** ship `return_td` now and add `return_yards` via a parallel §23.5 data task with the editor field code-gated (the C43 pattern); **(b)** block the editor build on adding the stat first; **(c)** drop return yards. Recommendation was (a).

**RULED 2026-08-16 (Chris): (a)** — his words: *"Ship with return TDs with the ability to easily add yards when we find a source."* **The emphasis on "easily" is folded in as a requirement on the design, not a hope:** §7.3.3.1's Special Teams bullet now spells the future data task as a 4-step checklist — (1) map the feed field in the provider adapter into `player_stats.advanced` (no migration, §23.5's storage rule); (2) add one `STAT_KEYS` entry (`return_yards`, `core_box`, `storage: 'advanced'`, `scoring_surface: 'scorable'`); (3) add the key to the Special Teams section catalog and flip its code gate on; (4) done — calculator, resolver, guardrails, and editor rendering are all key-agnostic. To keep step (3) trivial the editor renders sections **from the catalog** and the gated field is a catalog flag, never a hand-written form row. Nothing about the format, the snapshot, or scoring changes when it lands.

**Q11 — §7.2.1:190's notification recipient on the VOLUNTARY-LEAVE path: is the departing user notified, or only the commissioner? (filed by the M1 batch-15 remediation per R96, 2026-07-26; STOP-CONDITION HALT of R96's leave-path notification pin — the rest of the batch landed.)**

**Evidence.** §7.2.1's "Removal mechanics (all paths)" bullet at spec:190 reads: *"The removed user is notified with the outcome category (removed / left / franchise retired) and can be re-invited later — to any team, including their old franchise."* spec:192 then says *"Voluntary leave uses the same flow with `end_reason='left'`"*, which pulls the voluntary path INTO that bullet block. The parenthetical's three categories map to the §12.22 `end_reason` values that end a tenure (removed = `kicked`, left = `left`, franchise retired = `seat_retired`), and `left` is written by exactly ONE path in the repo: `leave_league` (063). Shipped behaviour: `remove_manager` notifies the REMOVED user on both takeover (`event: replaced`) and vacate (`event: removed`) — consistent with the bullet under either reading — while `leave_league` notifies **the sitting commissioner** ("A manager left <league>", `event: left`) and writes NOTHING to the departing user. The commissioner recipient is spec-silent: §7.2.1 never names the commissioner as a notification recipient anywhere (the nearest precedent is E54/spec:1734, "commissioner notified", for a near-simultaneous seat-claim collision — a different event, implemented in 062).

**Why this is a stop and not a Builder call.** Whether a user who just left gets a receipt is a PRODUCT decision (this file's §4 preamble routes product/scope calls to the spec changelog, not the decisions log), and both readings are defensible: **(a)** the block says "all paths", `left` can only mean the voluntary path, so the leaver IS a named recipient and the code omits a required notification; **(b)** "the REMOVED user" has no referent on a path where nobody was removed — the leaver performed the act synchronously and already has the RPC's success response, so the parenthetical is category VOCABULARY and the party who learns something new is the commissioner now holding an open seat. Under (a) the shipped code diverges from the spec; under (b) it is correct and the commissioner notification is a sanctioned addition. Pinning today's behaviour would silently cement (b) — precisely what R96's fix direction warned against.

**Options:**
- **(a) The leaver is notified too (recommended).** `leave_league` additionally calls the notifier for the departing user with the `left` category ("You left <league>"), keeping the commissioner notification as a spec-silent-but-useful addition recorded in the changelog. Correct under BOTH readings; ~6 lines plus one pin. The "it's noise" objection is real but bounded — §16's notification matrix (spec:1546) already defaults everything non-urgent to digests, and this is the least urgent class there is.
- **(b) Only the commissioner is notified (record the reading).** Rule that spec:190 addresses commissioner-initiated removals only; a one-clause §7.2.1 erratum says so and names the commissioner as the voluntary path's recipient. No code change — and the erratum is what stops this being re-found at every review.
- **(c) Both, with the leaver's as a digest-only receipt.** Needs a priority/digest flag `notifications` does not have, i.e. a new column for a row nothing consumes yet (F34: this notification has no consumer until L.A2.5/L.A2.7). Not recommended.

**Recommendation: (a)** — the only option correct under both readings, and smaller than the erratum (b) requires. Flagged as a product call because a notification's recipient set is very hard to change once a consumer exists.

**What's gated (precisely):** ONLY R96's leave-path notification pin, and any change to who `leave_league` notifies. Everything else in batch 15 landed on `feat/M1-L.A1.15-member-management`: R90–R95 and R97–R99 complete, full green proof chain, and R96's takeover/vacate row pins landed too (their recipient is the removed user under BOTH readings, so they cement nothing). **No task is blocked and no §5 blocker is filed** — the Q10 precedent for a question that gates a fix rather than a lane. L.A1.15 is done; the next lane heads (L.A2.x UI) do not consume this notification. Apply the ruling in whichever session next touches 063, or as a one-line PR; ledger row **F37** carries it.

**RULED 2026-07-26 (Chris): notify BOTH the user leaving AND the league manager (commissioner)** — recommendation (a), the reading correct under BOTH interpretations of §7.2.1:190. Applied same-day (M1 batch-16 remediation, same branch/PR #60): `leave_league` (063) now calls `notify_league_member_internal` for the departing user (`league_member` / "You left <league>" / `event: 'left'`) in addition to the pre-existing sitting-commissioner notification. **The deferred pin landed**: pgTAP 017 §S now pins BOTH the departing-user row and the commissioner row on §K's L1 leave (privileged 016-style read, `event='left'` scoped so it isolates from u5's earlier `removed` row). **Spec fidelity:** §7.2.1:190's "removed / left / franchise retired" categories already covered the departing user under reading (a) — now authoritative — but §7.2.1 named NO commissioner recipient anywhere, so the commissioner-too behaviour was spec-silent; folded in as spec erratum **v2.8.9** (§7.2.1:192 now names both recipients + changelog). **F37 flipped ✅**; the §5 Q11 note is cleared. Mechanics + the rest of batch 16 in D76.

**Q10 — `playoff_start_week` ↔ `regular_season_weeks` consistency: §7.3.1 promises a validation §7.3.8 never defines, and no formula fits the printed ranges (filed by the M1 batch-6 remediation per R62, 2026-07-22; substance observed by L.A1.6/D60(12), previously carried only as ledger row F25 — this entry puts it in the ruling queue).**

**Evidence:** §7.3.1's `playoff_start_week` row (D 15 · R 14–17 · note *"Validated against `regular_season_weeks`."*) promises a cross-field check, but §7.3.8's validation-bullet list contains no such bullet and prints no formula — and no formula is consistent with the printed ranges: strict continuity `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1` is **unsatisfiable at `regular_season_weeks = 12`** (would need start 13; the printed floor is 14) and makes start 17 unreachable (would need a 16-week regular season; the ceiling is 15), while anything looser permits **gap weeks** (e.g. regular 12 + start 17 → weeks 13–16 belong to neither the season nor the playoffs, and nothing defines what an idle league week IS — L.D0's schedule engine has no such concept). With no check at all — the shipped state — an **overlap** is expressible: `regular_season_weeks = 15` + `playoff_start_week = 14` parses clean and `validateLeagueSettings` accepts it (L.A1.6 implemented exactly the task-enumerated §7.3.8 bullets, deliberately not improvising a formula — D60(12)). The §7.3.8 arithmetic bullet (`start + rounds × weeks_per_round − 1 ≤ 18`) bounds the playoff END only; it says nothing about the seam.

**Options:**
- **(a) Strict continuity + range erratum (recommended).** Rule `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1`; spec erratum adjusts the printed R from 14–17 to **13–16** (13 reachable only at a 12-week season) and the schema range follows. No overlap, no gap weeks, no new concepts; the field becomes fully derived — the wizard can render it read-only next to `regular_season_weeks` (the `playoff_byes = 'auto'` precedent), with the stored value kept for §12.1 compat. Incumbent-consistent: ESPN/Yahoo/Sleeper all derive the playoff start; none lets a commissioner express an overlap.
- **(b) No-overlap lower bound only.** Rule `playoff_start_week ≥ regular_season_weeks + 1`; printed ranges stay. Kills the overlap but leaves gap weeks expressible, and gap-week semantics (standings? waivers? locks?) would then need defining somewhere before M4's schedule engine — a bigger spec debt than the seam check itself.
- **(c) Explicit won't-validate ruling.** Record that §7.3.1's note is aspirational in v1; the per-field ranges are the only guard and seam consistency is the commissioner's problem. Cheapest, but ships a settings surface that accepts playoffs starting before the season ends — and the note column then needs an erratum anyway (it currently promises otherwise).

**Recommendation: (a).** It is the only option with neither silent overlap nor undefined gap-week semantics; the cost is a two-line erratum (§7.3.1 R column + note, one §7.3.8 bullet) plus a ~6-line check in `validateLeagueSettings` with boundary pins — one small PR once ruled.

**What's gated (precisely):** NOT the current lane heads — engine is at L.A1.10 and schema at L.A1.11, neither touches playoff-week validation, so **no §5 blocker is filed**. The ruling gates **L.A1.12**: `create_league` (+ the L.A2.1 wizard on top of it) is the first surface that can PERSIST an inconsistent pair — creation must not ship on the unruled validator. L.A1.13's settings PATCH is the second exposure, not the first (the F25 row's original routing said L.A1.13 — corrected per R62). L.A1.6 itself remains complete; this question is bookkeeping mis-filed at first, not a new halt.

**RULED 2026-07-22 (Chris): option (a) — verbatim answer "a" — strict continuity `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1`.** Applied 2026-07-25 (branch `feat/M1-Q10-playoff-seam-ruling` — the "one small PR once ruled" this entry promised): spec erratum **v2.8.6** (§7.3.1 R column 14–17 → **13–16**, note now names the formula; ONE new §7.3.8 seam bullet — no overlap, no gap weeks; changelog carries the rationale: 13 reachable only at a 12-week season, 17 unreachable and dropped, incumbent-consistent, field effectively derived). Implementation: seam check in `validateLeagueSettings` with a per-field message + the 13–16 schema range in `league-settings.ts`; the old live-probe overlap pair (regular 15 + start 14) is now the pinned REGRESSION TRAP (exact message, sole error), all four boundary edges (12→13/13→14/14→15 defaults/15→16) pinned passing, one-past pinned failing both directions, and the check applies even at `playoff_teams = 0` — the field is derived, not conditional (D67(1); the D60(5) points-only skip covers only the playoff-END arithmetic bullet). Defaults (14+15) and the round-trip fixture (13+14) already satisfied (a) — pinned, no value change needed. The wizard's read-only-derived rendering (the `playoff_byes = 'auto'` precedent, stored value kept for §12.1 compat) is L.A2.1's build concern — ledgered as **F27**. B4 cleared; F25 flipped ✅; D67. **L.A1.12 unblocked.**

**Q9 — ESPN's verified in-product default kicking table (60+ FG tier) — and two D/ST micro-categories — cannot be expressed by the App B.4 catalog: ESPN template parity gap (filed by L.A1.9, 2026-07-21; STOP-CONDITION HALT per the task's re-verify rule — "Divergences from App B: stop and file a spec question").**

L.A1.9's build-time re-verification (task text item 1) ran the full sanctioned source pass on 2026-07-21 via the in-app browser (the L.A1.7 working path). **The F19 obligations themselves both RESOLVED cleanly** — evidence below, recorded here so no session refetches it — but the same pass surfaced a **new** App B divergence that the ESPN templates cannot express, and the task text is explicit that a divergence is a stop. No migration was written; nothing was seeded.

**What was retrieved (all 2026-07-21, in-app browser):**

1. **ESPN Scoring-Formats article** (support.espn.com/hc/en-us/articles/360003914032-Scoring-Formats) — re-fetched; standard PA table matches v2.8.3's transcription value-for-value (0/1–6/7–13/14–17/18–27/28–34/35–45/46+ at +5/+4/+3/+1/0/−1/−3/−5); the R50 finer custom-options PA list (2–6/18–21/22–27) still present, still values-free; nine YA buckets in custom options, **no standard YA values** (the F19(a) gap, reconfirmed). Standard offense: pass 0.04/TD 4/INT −2/2pt 2 · rush 0.1/6/2 · rec 0.1/6/2 (PPR +1/rec) · fumble lost −2 · KR/PR/fumble-recovery TD 6. **Standard kicking (the new finding): FG 0–39 = 3 · 40–49 = 4 · 50–59 = 5 · 60+ = 6 · PAT 1 · FG missed (any) = −1; no PAT-missed penalty.**
2. **ESPN D/ST article** (support.espn.com/hc/en-us/articles/115003847231) — re-fetched; split model reconfirmed ("D/ST begins each game with 10 points… given up 0 points (worth 5 points)… allowed 0 offensive yards (worth 5 points)") → the `def_ya_0_99 = +5` anchor. Also publishes two PAT micro-rules: **D/ST safety during a PAT = +1; D/ST returns the ball to its own end zone during a PAT = +2** (see finding 2 below).
3. **ESPN in-product defaults — the F19 pull (the product's own settings source, no auth):** `lm-api-reads.fantasy.espn.com/apis/v3/games/ffl/seasons/2026/segments/0/leaguedefaults/1?view=mSettings` (Standard) and `…/leaguedefaults/3?view=mSettings` (PPR). Full `scoringSettings.scoringItems` payloads, verbatim (statId, points, positional overrides — `{"16": v}` = applies to D/ST):
   - Standard (`leaguedefaults/1`): `[20,−2] [72,−2] [85,−1] [89,0,{16:5}] [90,0,{16:4}] [91,0,{16:3}] [92,0,{16:1}] [95,0,{16:2}] [96,0,{16:2}] [97,0,{16:2}] [98,0,{16:2}] [99,0,{16:1}] [123,0,{16:−1}] [124,0,{16:−3}] [125,0,{16:−5}] [128,0,{16:5}] [129,0,{16:3}] [130,0,{16:2}] [132,0,{16:−1}] [133,0,{16:−3}] [134,0,{16:−5}] [135,0,{16:−6}] [136,0,{16:−7}] [3,0.04] [24,0.1] [42,0.1] [86,1] [209,1,{16:1}] [19,2] [26,2] [44,2] [206,2,{16:2}] [80,3] [4,4] [77,4] [198,5] [25,6] [43,6] [63,6] [93,6,{16:6}] [101,6,{16:6}] [102,6,{16:6}] [103,6,{16:6}] [104,6,{16:6}] [201,6]`
   - PPR (`leaguedefaults/3`): identical **plus `[53,1]`** (receptions = 1) — nothing else differs.
   - Interpretation method (recorded for auditability — the payload is id-coded): the value multiset aligns one-for-one with the Scoring-Formats article's standard tables (offense 0.04/4/−2/2 · 0.1/6/2 · 0.1/6/2 · −2; PA +5/+4/+3/+1/−1/−3/−5 in the contiguous id runs 89–92 and 123–125; D/ST 2/2/2/2/1 + four 6-pt return TDs; kicking 3/4/5/6/1/−1), with **zero-valued buckets omitted from the payload** — PA 18–27 and YA 300–349 are exactly the article's 0-point rows and exactly the ids missing from the otherwise-contiguous runs. Two independent anchors pin the YA read: the head anchor `def_ya_0_99 = +5` (D/ST article) and the omitted-zero convention proven on the PA side.
   - **F19(a) RESOLVED — ESPN standard YA values (ids 128–136 in published-bucket order):** `<100 = +5 · 100–199 = +3 · 200–299 = +2 · 300–349 = 0 (omitted) · 350–399 = −1 · 400–449 = −3 · 450–499 = −5 · 500–549 = −6 · 550+ = −7`. Anchor matches. Unambiguous.
   - **F19(b) RESOLVED — the product's default model renders the STANDARD bucketization:** the default payload contains the standard list's ids (PA 1–6 present at +4; 18–27 absent-as-zero) and none of the finer custom-options buckets (no 2–6/18–21/22–27 items). The finer list is the LM custom bucket menu only; it is score-invisible at standard values as R50 recorded. The seeded def_pa keys stand; no additional keys needed; the templates (when they land) relate to the finer list as: not rendered by the default product, representable only in the v1.1 custom unlock (where F21's family-grouping applies).
4. **Yahoo SLN6489** (help.yahoo.com/kb/SLN6489.html) — full defaults retrieved (accordion DOM extraction): offense 0.04 (25 yds/pt) · pass TD 4 · **INT −1** · 0.1 rush/rec · TDs 6 · return TD 6 · off-fum-ret TD 6 · one combined 2-pt category = 2 · fumble lost −2 · **receptions 0.5 (the platform default = Half PPR, as §7.3.3 says)**; kicking FG 0–19/20–29/30–39 = 3 · 40–49 = 4 · 50+ = 5 · PAT 1 (**no miss penalties in defaults**; the sub-40 finer buckets are score-equal to `fg_0_39 = 3`); D/ST sack 1 · INT 2 · FR 2 · TD 6 · safety 2 · blocked kick 2 · KR/PR TD 6 · PA exactly the shared family: 0 = 10 · 1–6 = 7 · 7–13 = 4 · 14–20 = 1 · 21–27 = 0 · 28–34 = −1 · 35+ = −4 (single model, no YA — per spec). **Every Yahoo cell expressible in catalog keys; App B.1 Yahoo cells all reconfirmed.**
5. **Sleeper scoring-options article** (support.sleeper.com/en/articles/3998131-scoring-settings) — categories reconfirmed (PA = shared family buckets; YA buckets = ESPN's nine; FG buckets 0–19/20–29/30–39/40–49/50+, **no 60+ tier**) — but the article publishes **no default values**, and a support-center search ("default league settings") finds no Sleeper defaults article. Sleeper's in-product creation defaults sit behind account login (out of bounds). **Per the house verification rule (this task's charter): Sleeper's six template value-sets ship as App B best-known values FLAGGED unverified (ledger row on landing), never silently trusted.**

**The blocking finding (1): ESPN's default kicking table has a 60+ = 6 tier — App B.4's three-bucket shape (`fg_0_39`/`fg_40_49`/`fg_50_plus` at 3/4/5) cannot express it.** Product-confirmed twice, independently: the Scoring-Formats standard table (60+ = 6, 50–59 = 5) and both in-product default payloads (`[198,5]` = FG 50–59, `[201,6]` = FG 60+ — 198/201 are the only unaccounted 5/6-valued kicker ids, and their values match the article exactly). This is not a value drift on an existing key — it is a **category the engine's namespace cannot represent**: no `fg_50_59`/`fg_60_plus` keys exist, no columns exist, and — decisive — **the Sleeper feed has no 60+ signal** (`fgm_50p` aggregates everything ≥50; the L.A1.7 adapter audit lists sub-40 buckets but nothing above 50), so even new keys would have no data source on the current tier. Consequence: cent parity for ESPN templates is unachievable as-is on made 60+ FGs (order ~5–15 league-wide per NFL season; −1 pt each vs ESPN's product).

**The blocking finding (2), same class, smaller:** ESPN's defaults score two D/ST PAT micro-categories — PAT-safety = +1 (`[209,1,{16:1}]`) and PAT-return = +2 (`[206,2,{16:2}]`), both also published in the D/ST article. No catalog keys, no columns, no feed signal on any current provider tier (order ~1–3 plays league-wide per season).

**Why this is a stop and not an L.A1.7-style recorded erratum:** L.A1.7's charter explicitly licensed "seed what ESPN actually publishes and note the delta" (additive derived keys, no storage or feed dependency). L.A1.9's charter says the opposite — "Divergences from App B: stop and file a spec question (parity guarantee is the product promise — never silently ship drifted values)" — and this divergence has real options with product impact (below), including one that would add player_stats columns (schema beyond the task). Value-level per-platform differences (Yahoo's no-miss-penalty kicking, ESPN's no-PAT-miss) are NOT treated as divergences: B.1 defers K/D-ST to "each platform's own tables (⚠ verify)", so the verified platform table governs those cells; the stop is specifically for categories the catalog/namespace cannot express.

**Options:**
- **(a) Documented parity exception (recommended).** ESPN templates ship `fg_50_plus = 5`; the 60+ extra point and the two PAT micro-categories become a **named, documented parity exception** in §7.3.3/App B (spec changelog entry): "ESPN parity is cent-exact except made 60+ FGs (−1 pt vs ESPN) and D/ST PAT-safety/PAT-return (unscored) — categories the current data tier cannot observe." Rationale: the alternative keys would be **permanently pending/zero** for lack of any feed signal — a standing E61 state manufactured on every ESPN league every week is strictly worse than a documented ~1-pt/season-scale exception; and the parity guarantee's operative promise ("a migrating league's scores feel identical") survives a documented exception, not a standing honest-badge.
- **(b) Add `fg_50_59`/`fg_60_plus` (+ PAT-micro) keys and columns now.** Expresses the table, but no provider signal exists to fill them — every ESPN league shows permanent pending on those keys (E61), and it adds player_stats columns from inside a task chartered for `is_template` + seed only.
- **(c) = (a) + a September F-row:** the F10 raw-endpoint inspection window additionally checks whether Sleeper's raw feed carries a 60+ FG spelling (e.g. `fgm_60p`) and PAT-play detail; if a signal exists, upgrading ESPN kicking parity becomes the one-PR §23.5 data task it should be, and the exception shrinks or closes.
- **Recommendation: (a) + (c)'s September check.** One ruling line unblocks L.A1.9; the post-ruling build is mechanical (all six platforms' evidence is already in this entry).

**What's blocked:** L.A1.9 (migration 058 + pgTAP 012 + the 6 template rows) and the schema lane behind it (L.A1.11), plus L.A1.10/L.A1.12's template-row dependencies. **Not blocked:** L.A1.6 (engine lane, pure TS — still open and unstarted). F19 stays ⬜ Open (it discharges only when the ESPN rows land) but both its sub-obligations are answered above; the landing session should cite this entry in the 058 banner rather than refetching.

**RULED 2026-07-22 (Chris): option (a) + (c).** Ship `fg_50_plus = 5`; the ESPN 60+ FG tier (6 pts) and the two PAT micro-categories (+1 PAT-safety, +2 PAT-return) are **NAMED PARITY EXCEPTIONS**, not pending categories — recorded as a spec erratum (**v2.8.5**: §7.3.3 parity-guarantee erratum + App B.4 annotation + changelog) with the rationale (provider-unobservable, ~5–15 plays league-wide per season, permanent-pending would violate E61 semantics). **Condition:** the exceptions must be user-visible in the ESPN templates' description/detail metadata — a plain-language line a commissioner can read — not only in migration banners. **(c):** the September F10 check additionally looks for a Sleeper raw-feed 60+ spelling (e.g. `fgm_60p`) and PAT-play detail; if a signal exists, the tier becomes expressible as a one-PR §23.5 data task and the exception lifts — path noted in the erratum. Implementation: migration **058** + pgTAP **012** + `src/lib/leagues/scoring/templates.ts` (D59); the exception line lives in `scoring_systems.description` (the schema's existing detail column — a natural home, no schema change needed) and is pinned verbatim by pgTAP 012 and the templates tests. Sleeper's unpublished default values ship App-B-flagged per the house rule — ledger **F24**. B3 cleared; F19 flipped ✅.

**Q8 — client-writable league state: the spec-kept owner FOR ALL policy vs server-authoritative (§8.1) (filed by the M1 batch-2 review, R37/R38, 2026-07-20).** The review live-proved an ordinary authenticated user forging `scoring_rules_snapshot` + `status='drafting'` (and able to hard-DELETE a league, cascading `league_members`/`team_managers`) through 001's "League owners can manage" FOR ALL policy — which spec §12.1 explicitly said to keep — and a commissioner client-reseating `league_members.team_id` with no `team_managers` stint (cache⇄history divergence) through §12.2's printed commish FOR ALL policy.
**RULED 2026-07-20 (Chris): once created, league state is server-authoritative — no direct client DML.** Replace 001's "League owners can manage" FOR ALL with owner SELECT only (league creation already happens via RPC per the M1 task specs; the §15.1 deletion flow is a commish soft delete via RPC, so no client DELETE verb is retained — verified against the spec before implementing). Remove client UPDATE on `league_members` seating fields — reseating happens only via the L.A1.12–15 RPCs. The spec's "keep the owner policy" instruction is **superseded**: it predates 040's protected columns (`scoring_rules_snapshot`, `status`, `settings`), which turned a benign legacy policy into a forgery surface. Recorded in spec **v2.8.2**; implemented as migration **054** (D52).

**Q7 — Q4-application conflicts the conflict report didn't surface (filed 2026-07-20; STOP-CONDITION HALT of L.A1.1).** Recording the Q4 ruling (usernames 5–20, permanent) against the actual codebase hit two conflicts that C5 never surfaced, tripping the Builder session's ruling-vs-codebase stop condition — the migration was **not** written:

1. **AI persona accounts live in `profiles.username` with hyphenated handles** — `fieldscout-ai` (system owner) plus the ~19-persona roster (`bathew-merry-ai`, `zj-jachariason-ai`, …; `src/lib/personas/roster.ts`), created as real auth users + profiles rows by `scripts/seed-ai-personas.ts:88`, **existing in production** (the personas feature is live). *[Corrected — see D49(9)/R36: the roster personas are `ai_personas` rows, not profiles rows; only `fieldscout-ai` holds a profiles row. The conflict (and the ruling below) stands either way — the exempt pattern must cover every persona-shape handle a privileged writer seeds.]* A blocklist test *enforces* the `-ai` suffix (`blocklist.test.ts:41`), and the handles key avatar file paths + public URLs. Every one violates the `[a-z0-9_]` charset §7.2 gives the username contract — the CHECK as ruled would **fail the prod push** and break persona seeding. Needs your call: **(a)** exempt persona/system accounts — the CHECK becomes `human-pattern OR persona-pattern` (e.g. hyphenated, `-ai`-suffixed). Bonus: keeping hyphens out of the human charset means **no human can ever register a `*-ai` handle** — free namespace separation for the AI-transparency convention; **(b)** allow hyphens for everyone (loses that separation); **(c)** rename personas to underscores (touches public URLs, avatar files on disk, the blocklist tests, and any indexed content). **Recommendation: (a).**
2. **The account-settings page ships a live username-**change** flow** (`src/app/app/settings/page.tsx:173–181` — editable field, saves `username` with its own 3–30 validator), contradicting PERMANENT. Related definitional wrinkle: "no changing after creation" needs a boundary — signup *creates* the profile with an auto-generated `user_xxxxxxxx` placeholder, and the username-selection page (`/username`) is itself an UPDATE, so a literal no-update-after-creation guard would break onboarding. **Recommendation:** permanent = **after explicit selection** (the placeholder is pre-selection); remove the username field from settings (display-only `@handle`); typo/regret recovery is a support/admin path, not self-serve; a DB-level permanence guard is deferred until the selection flow moves server-side (an RPC that can tell selection from rename).
3. *(Minor, listed for completeness:)* `scripts/seed-dev-user.ts` seeds username `'dev'` (3 chars) — breaks under the 5-minimum; mechanical rename (e.g. `dev_user`/`dev_pro`) ships with the Q4 migration.

**What's blocked:** L.A1.1 (migration 040 carries the Q4 constraint per your ruling) and the serialized schema lane behind it. **Not blocked:** L.A1.6 (engine lane, pure TS). The Q5/Q6 rulings had no conflicts and are fully recorded/applied. One line from you on (1) and (2) unblocks the lane.
**RESOLVED 2026-07-20 (Chris): recommendations accepted for items 1, 2, and 3.** (1) Persona exemption **(a)**: the DB CHECK is `username ~ '^[a-z0-9_]{5,20}$' OR username ~ '^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*-ai$'` — human charset stays hyphen-free, so no human can register a `*-ai` handle (enforced at the DB layer by a 025-pattern guard trigger blocking persona-pattern usernames for `authenticated`/`anon`, since the CHECK alone can't tell a persona insert from a hostile PostgREST rename). (2) Permanent = **after explicit selection** — the signup-time `user_xxxxxxxx` placeholder is pre-selection and the `/username` page's UPDATE is the sanctioned selection write; the settings-page username field becomes **display-only**; typo/regret recovery is a support/admin path; a DB-level permanence guard is deferred until the selection flow moves server-side (documented residual: a determined user can still rename to a *valid human* name via direct PostgREST until then). (3) `seed-dev-user.ts` username `'dev'` → `'dev_user'`. Implementation: L.A1.1/040 (D49). B2 cleared.

**Q4 — username identity contract: §7.2 vs deployed reality vs spec-auth-profiles (filed per C5, 2026-07-20).** §7.2 requires `username` be **citext, 3–20 chars `[a-z0-9_]`**, and treats usernames as **changeable** ("league surfaces update live"; E52 tests a mid-season rename). Deployed reality: plain `TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL`, zero DB constraints; the only validation is a client-side regex allowing **3–30 chars, must start with a letter** (lowercased app-side at write); and `spec-auth-profiles.md` says usernames are **permanent in V1**. Three product calls needed: (a) do existing 21–30-char handles stay valid (grandfather) or get migrated? (b) citext conversion vs a `lower(username)` unique index? (c) changeable (per §7.2) or permanent (per auth spec) for v1? **Recommendation:** grandfather existing handles; enforce §7.2's charset + 3–20 length on *new/changed* usernames only (DB CHECK scoped via trigger on change); take the `lower(username)` unique index instead of a citext type migration (same case-insensitive semantics, no column rewrite); adopt §7.2's *changeable* contract — league surfaces join on `user_id` so renames are already safe, and the auth spec's "permanent" reads as a V1 simplification this epic supersedes (fold into both specs' changelogs on resolution). **M1 interim (D36, not gated on this):** invite-by-username matches via `lower(username)`; no column migration ships until you rule.
**RULED 2026-07-20 (Chris): usernames are minimum 5 characters, maximum 20, and PERMANENT (no changing after creation).** Supersedes both §7.2's 3–20/changeable contract and the deployed 3–30 client rule. No production users → no grandfathering: the DB constraint itself moves to 5–20 as part of the schema work (Builder's call on home: **folded into 040** — noted in tasks-M1 L.A1.1). Uniqueness stays case-insensitive via a `lower(username)` unique index (no citext conversion). Recorded in spec **v2.8** (§7.2 table + prose; E52 obsoleted). **Application halted same-session on Q7** (persona `*-ai` handles + the settings-page rename flow — neither surfaced by the conflict report); the ruling itself stands.

**Q5 — transactional email vendor for seat-targeted invites (filed per C6, 2026-07-20).** §7.2 makes email the **primary** invite channel ("a real email is sent with a claim link") — and the repo has **zero** outbound-email capability (no email lib, no edge functions, production SMTP commented out; only Supabase Auth's built-in mails + the local dev capture inbox). Needed from you: vendor choice, API key, and a `fieldscout.gg` sender domain (DNS records). **Recommendation:** Resend (Next.js-native, template-friendly, free tier covers beta). **M1 interim (D37, not gated on this):** the invite flow ships complete behind an `EmailSender` seam with a dev/log implementation (local capture inbox in dev), so flipping the real vendor on is config + a ~20-line adapter whenever the account exists.
**RULED 2026-07-20 (Chris): no email vendor is chosen now.** M1 builds invite email-sending behind a seam — **interface only, no vendor binding** (D37 confirmed as recommended). The v1 minimum bar, which must work regardless of vendor: **the league join link is always visible and copyable by the league manager**, so they can paste it into any email/text themselves (tasks-M1 L.A2.5 updated). Vendor selection deferred until the invite-send feature is ready to ship mail. Recorded in spec **v2.8**.

**Q6 — three doc edits only you should approve (filed per C1/C2/C13, 2026-07-20).** (a) **CLAUDE.md Key Business Rule #5** says "Leagues are Pro only. Gate league creation **and joining**" — the spec says joining is free (×3); any session following rule 5 literally would Pro-gate the join route and break §7.2. Edit to: "League **creation** is Pro only; joining is free." (b) **CLAUDE.md Redesign section** still says league/team/live-draft screens are "UI-only… do not invent API routes or schema" — stale since the epic was greenlit (M0 shipped schema; M1 ships routes). Scope it to non-greenlit surfaces or delete. (c) **spec-leagues-live-mode.md** contradicts the epic (join Pro-only, `commissioner_id`, thin schema) and §2.3 formally supersedes it, but the file carries no banner saying so — add one pointing at spec-redraft-leagues.md. **Recommendation:** all three are one-line edits; say the word and the next session applies them verbatim. M1 builds to the spec meanwhile.
**RULED 2026-07-20 (Chris), item (a) — and wider: NEITHER creating NOR joining a league requires Pro.** Supersedes §7.2's "Create league (Pro only)" and CLAUDE.md Business Rule #5, **rewritten this session** to: "League creation and joining are free. Pro-level league features come later." Spec swept in **v2.8** (§3.1 goal 6, §7.2, §15.1, §16 preamble, §17 matrix, §19.1, §20 metric retired, Appendix C L.A1); tasks-M1 de-Pro'd — **DoD changes flagged in-task**: L.A1.12 (requireProUser gate + in-body is_pro check + the non-Pro 402 `PRO_REQUIRED` test all deleted; replaced by "a free user creates successfully") and L.A2.1 (Pro upsell/402 state removed from the wizard). Items (b) CLAUDE.md redesign bullet and (c) spec-leagues-live-mode superseded banner were NOT ruled and stay open under the tasks-doc conflict report (C2/C13).

**Q3 — split D/ST model (`dst_model = 'split'`, ESPN): no canonical core_box stat keys (filed per R8, 2026-07-19).** The ESPN parity templates — 2 of the 6 v1 templates — score D/ST as "split +5 pts / +5 yds (start +10)" (spec App B comparison table; `dst_model = 'split'` per the App B kicking/D-ST note), which needs points-allowed *and yards-allowed* tier-indicator keys. The registry has zero yards-allowed keys and the spec names no canonical split-model keys (B.4 names only the single-model `def_pa_*` family). D21 covered middle-tier naming for the single model only; the Q2/v2.7 punt covers B.2–B.3, not this core_box gap. Not an M0 blocker, but M1's ESPN template-parity work lands on it. **Recommendation:** extend the D21 convention — keep `def_pa_<lo>_<hi>` as the shared points side and add a `def_ya_<lo>_<hi>` yards-allowed family on ESPN's own bucket boundaries (confirm the exact buckets from ESPN's published table when building the M1 parity fixtures); registry is additive, so the keys land with M1's template work once blessed. Needs Chris/Architect sign-off on the naming before M1 seeds them.
**RESOLVED 2026-07-19 (Chris): approved as recommended.** The ESPN split-D/ST model gets registry keys named `def_ya_<lo>_<hi>`, per the D21 convention and Appendix B.4; `def_pa_<lo>_<hi>` stays the shared points side. Exact ESPN bucket boundaries confirmed from ESPN's published table when M1 builds the parity fixtures. Seeding the actual keys belongs to whichever task next touches the stat-key registry (registry is additive) — resolution recorded here, no keys seeded with it. Fold into the spec changelog when the keys land.

**Q1 — `sleeper_free` can't meet the live-provider hard requirements (kickoff timestamps + official inactives).** Spec §23.1 makes official inactives ~90 min pre-kickoff and in-game injury designations a hard requirement of whichever *live* provider runs, and §23.3 derives every lock from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at evaluation time — but the free Sleeper schedule endpoint is day-granularity only, there is no official-inactives feed in the current integration, and nothing writes `nfl_games`.
**RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (Chris): proceed with nflverse.** `sleeper_free` stays the stats source; nflverse supplements kickoff timestamps (and is the likely official-inactives source). Engineering notes (D16): the nflverse adapter lands with the first runtime consumer of kickoffs (locks/schedule milestone — not M0); nflverse schedule/inactives data is retroactively fetchable, so the 2026 fixture library can be back-filled at any time — accepted limitation: back-fill loses real *arrival timing* of the ~90-min-pre-kickoff inactives publication (synthetic scenarios cover that timing per §23.1). M0's recorder proceeds as specced.

**Q2 — canonical advanced stat-key names: §23.5 vs Appendix B conflict.** §7.3.3's dot-product requires one shared key namespace, but §23.5 says `air_yards`/`yards_after_catch` while Appendix B.2 scores `receiving_air_yards`/`receiving_yac`.
**RESOLVED 2026-07-18 (Chris): punted — the named advanced stats were examples, not v1 commitments.** Misunderstanding corrected: air yards / YAC / yards-after-contact in §23.5/Appendix B are **illustrative** of the long-run advanced-scoring direction, contingent on raising money and funding a paid real-time stats API (or building one). No canonical naming decision is needed now. Consequences: M0 seeds `STAT_KEYS` with `core_box` only; the `tracking`/`charted` **tier machinery** (capability tiers, two-phase settle, revision handling — the §7.3.3 extensibility contract, which *is* v1-committed) is proven with clearly-marked placeholder keys (D15); real keys become a one-PR data task when funded (§23.5 checklist). Recorded in spec changelog **v2.7**; M1's Alpha/Ultra backtest exit criterion deferred (delivery plan **v1.3**). **Follow-up resolved same day (Chris): the v1 template picker ships the 6 parity templates only** — no Alpha/Ultra teaser cards; the FieldScout cards and the "same game, scored three ways" widget return when advanced stats are funded (spec §7.3.3/§16/App B/App C annotated).

## 4. Decisions log

*Build-time engineering decisions made during implementation that aren't spelled out verbatim in the spec — naming, library choices, minor sequencing calls. Product/scope decisions belong in the spec's own changelog (see spec-redraft-leagues.md), not here; this log is for "how we built it," not "what we're building."*

**2026-08-17 — Architect (the draft-room redesign breakdown, PR #155 — merged 2026-08-17; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-DR-draft-room-redesign.md` §3 per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 / tasks-M3 D126–D143 precedent.** *Folded late, by the **DR.1** Builder on 2026-08-18: PR #155's own §6 owed this transcription "at merge" and the merge landed without it, so §4 ran D146 → D157 with the ten numbers D157 had just been renumbered around. Discharged here rather than left for DR.2 to trip over — the same PR also files the §6 row #155 owed, as **F63**.)*

- **D147 — The room escapes the shell by moving the guard up, not by duplicating it.** `src/app/app/layout.tsx` today does auth + username gate + `<AppShell>` in one component (:12–40). It splits: the **layout keeps the guards and becomes a pass-through**, and `<AppShell>` moves down into a route group `src/app/app/(shell)/layout.tsx` that holds every existing route, with the room in a sibling group `src/app/app/(room)/leagues/[leagueId]/draft/`. **Route groups do not affect URLs**, so `/app/leagues/[id]/draft` is unchanged — no redirect, no link rewrite, no broken deep link, and the `DraftBar`'s own-room path check keeps working. Chosen over the alternatives deliberately: a `usePathname()` conditional inside `AppShell` would make every app route pay for the room's special case and would still mount the shell's providers; a separate top-level `/draft/…` URL would break every shipped link and the spec's §16.1 route table. **The guard is not duplicated into two layouts** — one copy, above both groups, is what keeps cold-load auth honest (D148).
- **D148 — Cold-load correctness is an acceptance criterion with a named adversary.** A new browser tab is a server-rendered cold start with no client history, and so is a refresh mid-draft; the new-tab ruling makes this the *primary* path rather than an edge case. **Observation recorded 2026-08-17 (Chris, in two browsers):** loading the live draft URL directly bounced to `/app?redirect=%2Fapp%2Fleagues%2F…%2Fdraft` while in-app click-through worked. Two mechanisms exist and the Builder must distinguish them by evidence rather than assume:
  **(a) the dev-auth artifact (likely, and benign in production).** `devAutoLogin` (`src/lib/supabase/dev-auth.ts:26–45`) is a **client-side** `signInWithPassword`. On the very first cold load of a fresh browser there is no session cookie yet, so the server sees an anonymous request and `middleware.ts:36–42` redirects; the browser then signs in, and every later request has a cookie. That produces exactly the observed two-hop shape (`/app/leagues/…/draft` → `/login?redirect=…` → middleware's :45–50 branch sees a user, rewrites the pathname to `/app` and **keeps the search params** because it clones `nextUrl`, landing on `/app?redirect=…`).
  **(b) a real, production-plausible defect found while diagnosing (a).** `src/middleware.ts` writes refreshed auth cookies onto `supabaseResponse` via `setAll` (:18–27) but **both redirect branches return a brand-new `NextResponse.redirect(...)` (:41 and :49), which does not carry those cookies.** This is the documented `@supabase/ssr` footgun: a cold load holding an expired-but-refreshable token can be bounced *and* lose the refresh. It is not reachable through in-app client-side navigation, which is exactly why the redesign — whose primary entry is a cold tab — is what would surface it.
  **The task's obligation is to prove which one it is, on a real (non-dev-auth) session, and to leave a test rather than a memory** (DR.1, DR.8). Filed as ledger row **F63** so the routing is findable. *(Transcription correction, DR.1 2026-08-18: this sentence read **F61** when the breakdown was authored, and the entry's own §6 marked the number provisional per R312 first-filed-keeps. PR #156 filed F61/F62 first, so this row is **F63** — the number D158(4) reserved for exactly this re-point. Nothing else in this decision changed.)* *(Recorded but out of scope to celebrate: `login/page.tsx:24/:51` does honor `?redirect=`, so once a user logs in they do land in the room — the destination is preserved through the login page and lost only by middleware's `/login → /app` rewrite.)*
- **D149 — Three zones, two bands of chrome, and the on-the-clock line resolves INTO the status strip rather than becoming a third band.** The brief flagged three candidates competing for the top (the 54px bar, the Live/Round/order strip, and the on-the-clock line). They resolve to **two**: the command bar (54px, ink, pinned) and the status strip (`h-header` = 58px, the existing token). Chris's "move it to the left side of **the div**" is read as the div it already lives in — the status strip's flex row (`snake-draft-room.tsx:719–765`), where it currently sits **right-aligned next to the clock** (:743–759). Moving it left makes one band whose two ends read *whose turn* and *how long*, which is a better answer than a dedicated band and costs 112px of vertical chrome instead of ~170px. **A third band is out of scope and a Builder proposing one has left it.**
- **D150 — The dock is a NON-MODAL drawer, and that single choice settles most of its behavior.** The panels overlay the board; the board, the clock, the command bar and the presence strip stay visible and operable behind them. Therefore: **no focus trap, nothing `inert`, no scroll lock, no backdrop that swallows clicks** — a user must be able to watch the clock while browsing the pool, which is the entire draft-night workflow. Escape closes; clicking the active tab toggles it closed; **exactly one panel is open at a time** (two open panels is a rail again). Focus moves to the panel on open and **returns to the tab button** on close. Default state is **closed**. **This is deliberately NOT the shipped `Sheet`/Radix Dialog primitive**, which traps focus and marks the rest of the page inert by design — using it here would make the board unreadable while the pool is open. The dock is a plain positioned region with `role="tabpanel"`/`aria-expanded` wiring, not a modal.
- **D151 — Open height is fixed, and the board never resizes.** The open panel occupies a fixed fraction of the viewport (`min(60vh, …)` desktop / ~75vh mobile — the Builder pins the exact token) and is **absolutely positioned over** the board. The board's own geometry — the grid's `minmax(96px, 1fr)` columns and its horizontal scroll (`draft-board-grid.tsx:53–105`) — **must not change when a panel opens or closes**: a board that re-lays-out on every tab press is the thing a full-width board was asked for to avoid. No drag-to-resize in v1 (a resize handle on a drawer that overlays a horizontally-scrolling grid is a pointer-conflict problem worth its own task, not a freebie).
- **D152 — Elevation: the dock panels and the command bar are BOTH sanctioned resting shadows, and each says why in a comment.** CLAUDE.md's ruling is that nothing in normal flow rests elevated and shadows appear only behind an interaction prefix — **with an explicit exception for true overlays and for bars pinned over scrolling content**. The dock panels are true overlays (they float above the board); the 54px command bar is pinned chrome over scrolling content. Both therefore keep a resting `shadow-hard-*` **with a comment naming the exception**, exactly as `src/components/ui/elevation-rule.test.ts:38`'s `OVERLAY_FILES` allowlist requires of shared primitives — and any new file the test's sweep covers is added to that allowlist with its reason, never silenced. **Everything else the redesign touches obeys the ordinary rule:** the status strip does not rest elevated, and selected/on-the-clock/active states stay carried by fill (`bg-accent-soft`) or border (`border-accent`), never by a shadow.
- **D153 — `Draft Options` is a menu over the SHIPPED panel body, not a reimplementation of it.** CLAUDE.md forbids near-duplicate components, and `commish-draft-panel.tsx` is 956 lines of working, reviewed, refusal-aware controls. The menu lists the control groups; choosing one opens the existing panel at that section. **What actually changes in that file is its trigger** — the blue `Commish panel` button (:120–123) is deleted and the panel becomes trigger-less, opened by the bar. The eight sections keep their bodies, their gates, their confirm dialogs and their system-post semantics. **Nothing about §8.7's control semantics changes in this lane** — no new refusal, no relaxed one, no altered audit or chat behavior.
- **D154 — On a mock, the command bar is the launcher's bar, because a mock has no commissioner.** `isCommish` is already `false` on every mock (`snake-draft-room.tsx:443`, D110(1)). The bar's three variants are therefore: **commissioner** (Pause/Resume + Draft Options + status + Exit), **member** (status + Exit), **mock** (MOCK identity + status + Exit, plus — for `config.mock.launched_by` only — Pause/Resume practice and a reduced *Practice options* menu carrying delete-and-exit). The `MockBanner` at `:712` is **absorbed into the bar** rather than stacked beneath it (§16.5.4's v2.12 note): a permanent bar plus a permanent banner saying the same thing is the duplication §16.3's say-a-thing-once rule exists to stop. **No commissioner control becomes reachable on a mock** — the reduced menu carries only what D110(1) already permits the launcher.
- **D155 — The pause overlay stops narrating and starts illustrating.** With the bar announcing "Draft paused by @commish" for everyone, `DraftPauseOverlay`'s duplicate copy is retired; the board keeps a *visual* paused treatment (dimmed, non-interactive) and the clock keeps its shipped paused rendering (`pick-clock.tsx`'s paused mode). **The Resume affordance moves to where the actor is** — the bar's Resume button for a commissioner, the same for a mock's launcher — so `canResume`/`onResume` (`pause-overlay.tsx:38`, wired at `snake-draft-room.tsx:604`) lose their button rather than their meaning. One state, one voice, one place to act.
- **D156 — The two-tabs guard is a courtesy over a correctness boundary, and is scoped to say so.** *(**RULED by Chris 2026-08-17** — "The most recent one takes over and the others disconnect"; PROGRESS §3 **Q14** Resolved. This decision is now built, not proposed.)* The server is authoritative (§8.1), so two tabs can never corrupt a draft — a stale tab's action is refused by the same validators as anyone else's. What two tabs *do* cost is real but bounded: two sockets and two `draft:<id>` subscriptions against §9.3's ≤3-channel budget, two `draft_touch` heartbeats, and a presence list that shows one manager twice (presence is keyed by team id — `use-draft.ts:244`). The guard is therefore **client-local leader election** (`BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id, `localStorage` fallback): newest tab holds the room, older tabs unsubscribe, stop the heartbeat, and render a takeover state. **Per browser profile, not per user** — a laptop and a phone are two legitimate clients and are left alone. **It adds no channel, no route, no server state.**

- **D157 — L.C1.3 build mechanics (migration 085).** (1) **THE E2 MECHANISM IS THE OPENING BID ROW, and it is the same row for both verbs.** The task left the choice open ("`draft_bids` opening row or a config echo"); `draft_nominate` writes the opening bid to `draft_bids` exactly like a raise, so §12.5 carries one uniform history, the room's bid feed needs no special case, and both RPCs replay through ONE lookup — `SELECT … FROM draft_bids WHERE draft_id = … AND action_id = …` under the draft-row lock, the 066:917 select-then-insert pattern. It is **never** an `ON CONFLICT` upsert: `uniq_draft_bid_action` is PARTIAL and a bare arbiter raises 42P10 (D144(7)/R310, read before writing rather than discovered at runtime). Replay semantics inherit R125 verbatim — an action_id is consumed forever, no `is_undone` or phase filter — and 034 pins the consequence that matters: a replayed NOMINATION during the BIDDING phase returns its original row instead of the phase refusal, which is exactly the reconnect case E2 exists for and would fail if the replay arm sat below the validations. (2) **D126's phase rule needed two readings the spec does not print, and both are recorded and pinned.** Through the BIDDING phase `on_clock_team_id` stays the NOMINATOR (it is the seat 086's rotation advances FROM, and the room's "X nominated" attribution), and `current_pick_number` is NOT consumed by opening a nomination — it is that nomination's sequence number until the award. Both are pinned in 034, and where the file needs a second nomination it performs a PRIVILEGED "simulated close" (clear `current_nomination`, bump the sequence by hand) with a comment saying so, because a pin that leaned on 086's award arm would be pinning code that does not exist yet. (3) **Anti-snipe is implemented as `deadline := GREATEST(deadline, now() + anti_snipe)`, with the zero case as its own branch.** GREATEST states D128 as "the clock may only be EXTENDED": above the threshold the standing deadline wins (the countdown continues — Chris's own clarification), at the threshold the two are equal, below it the floor wins. The `auction_anti_snipe_seconds = 0` case is a separate branch on purpose — **and the reason was recorded WRONG at first landing; corrected in the batch-3 fix cycle (R329).** It is NOT that GREATEST would hand an expired clock "a fresh now()-based clock": at anti_snipe 0, `now() + make_interval(secs => 0)` IS now(), so the two forms agree on every LIVE deadline and `GREATEST(expired, now())` is merely now() — still due, not fresh. The branch is observable in exactly two states, both of which are the disabled extension declining to touch a clock: an ALREADY-EXPIRED deadline, which an unconditional GREATEST would REWRITE forward to now() (pinned, 034 pin 61, and it is the ONLY pin the probe reddens), and a NULL one, which GREATEST — ignoring NULLs — would INVENT (unreachable today: nominate always writes a deadline and the one NULL-deadline state is `paused`, which both verbs refuse first). **The counterpart is now recorded rather than silent:** with anti_snipe > 0 a bid landing after the clock already read zero receives a FULL FRESH WINDOW (`now() + anti_snipe`) — D128's letter, and consistent with snake's posture that the TICK is the enforcer of expiry, not the deadline column; pinned at 034 pin 62. **The exact-threshold instant is observationally a no-op** (flooring to 10s when 10s remain changes nothing), so the discriminating pins are threshold − 1s (floors) and threshold + 1s (does not), both pinned to the second against the transaction instant. (4) **The max-bid clause IS §8.6.8 at the bid layer, and it is pinned by its CONSEQUENCE, not only by its refusal.** Bids move no money (D131(2)), so no bid can break solvency; an AWARD of an over-large bid can. `max_bid = remaining − (open_slots − 1) × min_bid` is precisely the largest amount whose award leaves the winner exactly on the floor — so 034 simulates the award AT max_bid (solvent, at equality) and ONE DOLLAR ABOVE it (insolvent), and carries the cross-cutting property "no bid above its bidder's max bid exists in history", bracketed by a population count so the NOT EXISTS cannot pass over an empty table (R307). (5) **Validation ORDER is a UX decision, recorded: capacity is checked BEFORE the bid bounds.** A complete roster reads `max_bid` 0 (084's E27 branch), so bounds-first would refuse a full team with "over your max bid of $0" instead of "your roster is complete" — the message would be true and useless. (6) **MOCK AUCTIONS ARE REFUSED BY BOTH VERBS — a deliberate seam, not an omission (F61).** No auction mock can exist today (071's `create_mock_draft` refuses auction configs and a mock's `draft_type` is snapshotted at creation), so the refusal is unreachable; the alternative was silence, and silence becomes a hole the moment L.C1.7 lifts the 071 refusal — every league member could bid inside another member's solo practice until the D103(2) launcher gate is retrofitted. Bidder-team resolution for mock seats is genuinely L.C1.7's design (CPU seats bid through the tick, D132), so the seam refuses now and lifts there, with the two 034 pins flipping in that PR. Its sibling obligation is **F62**: 086's system nomination must keep the invariant 085 establishes — every nomination opens with a `draft_bids` row (`action_id` NULL for the system path, which is why C39 made the column NULLable). (7) **PROBE-ORDERING DISCIPLINE — learned by running the DoD probe twice.** The first shape of 034 put the E5 over-max refusal in the MIDDLE of a bid ladder; under the probe the refused bid landed, the next pin's bid became a self-raise, and that raised an ERROR outside `throws_ok` which **aborted the file at 42 of the then-84 asserts with a single RED** — the probe destroyed the evidence it was supposed to produce. Reordering so that each ladder's over-max refusal is its LAST act and comes from a seat that is NOT the standing high bidder gives the honest signature: **6 of 91 RED and the file runs to the end** (the count re-captured against the batch-3 plan; §F's new R330 identity block obeys the same discipline — its ACCEPTED arm first, both refusals from seats that are not the standing high bidder — which is why its own probe leaves 5 RED instead of aborting), including the property pin and the two population counts that show the refused bids landed. *Rule to carry forward: a break probe that aborts the suite proves less than one that leaves its wreckage on the floor to be counted — order the pins so the mutation's damage stays observable.* (8) **Recorded residual (no bespoke message):** a RETIRED seat's manager reaching a bid path would get 084's loud P0002 from `draft_team_budget` (R321) rather than a bespoke refusal. (9) **Break-probe results AS RUN (the R306 lesson), all three re-captured against the batch-3 plan of 91:** (a) the DoD probe — dropping `IF p_amount > v_max_bid` — turned **6 of 034's 91** pins RED: 48 (LA's $187 vs a $186 max), 81 (E25's $2 vs a $1-max seat), 87 (the same at min_bid 0), 66 and 88 (the two population counts: the refused bids landed), and **89**, the property pin — plus **2 of 3** cases in the wire suite. (b) the R330 probe — removing the nomination-identity guard — turned **5 of 91** RED (44, 45 the two refusal arms; 46 the per-nomination row count; 66 and 88 the population counts), with pin 43 (the matching-identity ACCEPTANCE) GREEN by construction. (c) the R329 probe — replacing the zero branch with an unconditional GREATEST — turned **exactly 1 of 91** RED (pin 61), with pin 60 GREEN, which is the finding it was written for. All reverted; 91/91 and 3/3 re-verified. (10) **NOMINATION IDENTITY ON THE BID PATH (R330 — landed in the batch-3 fix cycle, before 085 ever merged).** `draft_place_bid` gained two OPTIONAL trailing arguments, `p_nomination_seq` and `p_player_id`, refusing on mismatch with §16.3's "just went off the board" copy; omitted ⇒ shipped behavior, so no caller broke. **Why the RPC and not the route:** the RPC is the server-authoritative boundary (spec §4/§8.1 — clients never compute, and every caller must be safe, not only HTTP ones); a route guard would leave the sim, the pgTAP suite and every future caller exposed, and L.C1.4's completion path awards on exactly this data. **Why BOTH arguments:** neither subsumes the other — `player_id` catches the ordinary moved-on case, and `nomination_seq` catches the two cases where the same player is live under a different nomination (D143's cancel-and-renominate does NOT consume the sequence number; an undone award returns a player to the pool at a later sequence). (11) **RECORDED RESIDUAL — the E2 replay lookup is VERB-BLIND (R331, ledger row F65).** Both verbs replay on `(draft_id, action_id)` with no verb discrimination, so an action_id used by one verb returns a false success through the other (proven live). The contract is therefore per-verb and enforced at the MINT SITE (L.C2.1), and the three in-body shapes were each rejected with a stated reason: **narrowing** the lookup is forbidden because the UNQUALIFIED lookup under the draft lock is exactly what makes a duplicate action_id un-insertable (it is the recorded reason no `EXCEPTION WHEN unique_violation` wrapper is owed, and narrowing re-opens a raw 23505 on the PARTIAL `uniq_draft_bid_action`); **argument-consistency** discrimination contradicts R125 and the two shipped 034 E2 pins, which deliberately replay with DIFFERENT arguments and assert the original row comes back; and **position-based verb inference** ("an opening row is the earliest row of its nomination_seq") breaks under D143's cancel-and-renominate, which writes a second opening under an existing seq and would make the rule FALSE-REFUSE a legitimate reconnect retry in L.C1.5's world — a worse bug than the one it closes. A verb column on `draft_bids` would settle it exactly and is recorded as the option rather than taken (085 ships no DDL, and the table is L.C1.1's).
