## Review findings — 2026-07-27 (M1 batch 20)

**Findings-remediation Builder session on `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page` (PR #66 — fix-then-merge, no new PR). One should-fix (R114) from the PR #66 review: the join-by-code dialog dead-ended on a pasted `/join/…` link — the exact affordance its own copy advertises. Purely input-normalization on the join-by-code entry; the F2 surface, the six-state claim logic and the v2.8.10 erratum are untouched.**

### Should-fix

- **R114 · should-fix · `src/components/leagues/leagues-index.tsx`:65** — the join-by-code dialog breaks on a pasted `/join/…` link, the exact affordance its own copy advertises. *Evidence:* the submit handler does `router.push(\`/join/${encodeURIComponent(trimmed)}\`)`, passing the whole pasted string verbatim as the `[token]` param with no code/token extraction. But the dialog's DialogDescription tells the user to "paste a fieldscout.gg/join/… link" and the label reads "Invite code or link". The real share artifacts ARE full absolute URLs: `buildJoinLink` (invite-panel-ops.ts:264) returns `${origin}/join/${codeOrToken}`; the wizard copy button (league-create-wizard.tsx:996) copies `${window.location.origin}/join/${result.invite_code}`. `encodeURIComponent('https://fieldscout.gg/join/a1b2c3d4e5')` yields the single unresolvable segment `/join/https%3A%2F%2F…`; `get_join_preview` matches only exact token / lower(invite_code) / lower(invite_slug), so a full URL → `{found:false}` → "This link isn't valid" on a VALID invite. Typing a bare code works; pasting a link (an explicitly-offered input) dead-ends. F2 intact, no security issue. *Fix direction:* before pushing, if the input contains `/join/`, take the last non-empty path segment (strip query/hash) and encodeURIComponent only that; otherwise use the trimmed value as-is.

### Resolution — 2026-07-27 (Builder, same branch `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page`, PR #66)

| Finding | Resolved by |
|---|---|
| R114 (should-fix) | this commit — extraction lifted into a PURE helper `extractJoinCode` in `invite-panel-ops.ts` (the §7.2 share-link section, directly beside `buildJoinLink` as its exact inverse — NOT buried in the dialog's onClick), and `JoinLeagueDialog.handleSubmit` + the Continue-button `disabled` gate now push/enable on `extractJoinCode(code)` instead of the raw trim. The helper trims, cuts everything from the first `?`/`#`, then takes the last non-empty path segment after a case-insensitive `/join/` marker; a bare code/slug (no `/join/`) passes through trimmed. It keeps the segment's original case (seat tokens are case-sensitive; the RPC lower()s codes/slugs itself) and does NOT URL-encode — the caller still `encodeURIComponent`s the route param. Pinned in `invite-panel-ops.test.ts` §8: a 16-row table (full absolute URL, bare-host, protocol-relative, path-only, trailing slash, `?query`, `#hash`, query+slash, custom-slug link, whitespace-wrapped link, bare-code + bare-slug passthrough, empty + whitespace-only) **including the two REAL share artifacts** — `buildJoinLink('https://fieldscout.gg', CODE)`'s own output and the wizard's `${origin}/join/${invite_code}` shape — plus a case-preservation pin (mixed-case token unchanged) and an empty-code pin (`/join/` with no segment → `''`, so the dialog no-ops rather than pushing a dead segment). **Break probe shown:** helper body forced to `return raw.trim()` (the pre-R114 verbatim passthrough) → **exactly 14 of the table rows fail** (every link form), while the bare-code and empty rows STAY green — proving the table discriminates the fix rather than passing vacuously; reverted, re-proven green. **D39 browser pass (pre-auth, cheap):** against a seeded local league (`invite_code='r114probe1'`, `status='setup'`, 12 seats), navigated the EXACT URLs `router.push` targets before vs. after — `/join/https%3A%2F%2Ffieldscout.gg%2Fjoin%2Fr114probe1` (the OLD verbatim-encoded target) renders "This link isn't valid" (the bug reproduced on a valid invite); `/join/r114probe1` (the extracted bare code the NEW helper produces) renders the real "R114 Probe League · 12 seats open" claimable card. `get_join_preview` confirmed the same split at the RPC (`{found:true,status:ok}` on the bare code vs. `{found:false}` on the full URL). The authed dialog-click on `/app/leagues` could not be walked in this session (a local GoTrue seed-auth limitation — the hand-seeded user's client login didn't complete its post-sign-in redirect under automation; an environment constraint, not R114), so the observable behavior was verified at the pre-auth route it feeds — the dialog's onClick is a three-line wiring of the unit-pinned helper into `router.push`, and the URL it produces (`/join/r114probe1`) is exactly the one shown resolving. All seeded rows CLEANED (0 leagues/users/profiles/identities after teardown). Proofs: `test` 37 files / **684** (stack up; invite-panel-ops 33→**39**) · `test:gate` **24** · `type-check` clean · `lint` pre-existing-only. **D81** |

### ADDENDUM — 2026-08-13 (M2 batch 17 re-review: R285–R286, second fix round on PR #145)

**The re-review of the batch-17 remediation surfaced one BLOCKER + one should-fix in the PR's new stack suite (`draft-board-autopick-db.test.ts`); both resolved on the SAME branch. The batch-17 record's "no deterministic branch-caused failure, the PR's proof chain stands" clause is RETRACTED as recorded-wrong — corrected in place at the R282 bullet above and in the F52 row's batch-17 clause.**

- **R285 · should-fix · `cleanup()` swallowed every error — one failed players-DELETE left 20 toxic fixture rows in the shared pool permanently — TAKEN** — the reviewer reproduced it twice from clean state: league/user/list rows gone, zero referencing rows remaining, yet 20 `bap-wire%` rows persisted — the players delete had failed at a moment references existed (23503; `draft_picks`/`league_rosters`/`draft_queues` player FKs are NO ACTION) and the unchecked `await service.from('players').delete()` swallowed it (the D114(7)/F53 class + CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'"). **Resolved:** EVERY fixture write/read in the file now throws through one `throwIfError` gate — cleanup (stale-league lookup, drafts/teams/leagues/players deletes), `deleteUserByUsername` (lookup + deleteUser), beforeAll (players upsert, scoring-template lookup), and the file's other swallow-vulnerable reads (the rewind UPDATE, post-tick status read, `readPicks`, the step-3 queue read — where an ERRORED read previously rendered as "no rows" and would have PASSED the discriminator for exactly the wrong reason — the round-2 player read, the final league-status read). **Probe A SHOWN:** league-graph deletes disabled → the run FAILED loudly (`cleanup: players delete failed: … violates foreign key constraint "draft_picks_player_id_fkey"` — the reviewer's exact moment, previously a silent pass + toxic rows) → reverted → the NEXT run's beforeAll cleanup cleared the probe's own poisoned state (5 rows + 1 league) and went green: recovery from a poisoned pool is now part of the suite.
- **R286 · BLOCKER · the fixture band adp 0.01–0.20 captured the GLOBAL source-4 walk — co-scheduled suites' autopicks drew `bap-wire-*` rows, R285 made it persistent, and the batch-17 "no deterministic branch-caused failure" clause was therefore recorded-wrong — TAKEN, all three arms** — 068's source-4 walk is global (`ORDER BY pl.adp NULLS LAST, pl.id` over the SHARED players pool) and 0.01–0.20 strictly dominated every neighbor, so `draft-realtime-db.test.ts:341`'s in-fixture-set assert (its band is `adp: i + 1`) lost to ours whenever the windows overlapped. **(a)** R285's loud cleanup landed (kills the persistent arm). **(b) Fixture redesign — the reasoning recorded:** no reachable band is safe by construction — a dominating band captures every co-scheduled walk, an integer band ties nondeterministically with real values (the suite's own pre-band observation: three different adp-7 tie winners), and fixtures cannot be steered around source 4 because 068 gates sources 1–3 on `v_user IS NOT NULL` (placeholder seats ALWAYS walk ADP). The fixtures now carry **`adp: NULL`** — NULLS LAST puts them behind the ENTIRE real pool, the one placement NO walk (this league's or any co-scheduled suite's) can reach — which makes the board discrimination STRONGER (any fixture pick MUST be the board speaking) and shrinks the set 20 → 5 (board-only). The demote-arm assert is now STRUCTURAL instead of the exact-id `adpBest` pin (the ADP fallback walks the LIVE pool — data-dependent winner): not-a-fixture + the board's next entry still available AND unpicked (nothing but a board read can reach it) + the picked player carries a real ADP (the source-4 signature) + exactly ONE fixture on the whole 16-pick sheet (the round-1 board pick); §8.4's priority order itself stays pinned in pgTAP 022. **Existence window narrowed** per the fix direction: players upsert + board-list creation moved INTO the test body immediately before attach/`draft_start`; released in a `finally` (league graph first — the NO ACTION player FKs — then players) so even an assertion-failure path releases; the afterAll belt kept. Sequencing db suites apart NOT taken: vitest's default parallel file scheduling makes that a repo-wide harness change — the L.B7.1 sweep's, not this fix round's. **Probe B SHOWN (the mechanism on demand):** ONE dominating row (`bap-wire-probe0`, adp 0.01) inserted → `draft-realtime-db.test.ts:341` RED (`expected false to be true` — its autopick drew the probe row) → row deleted → green 2/2. **(c)** Records corrected: the F52 row's batch-17 clause (retraction + mechanism named), the R282 bullet (inline retraction note), and the durable ADP-space/suite-isolation design question added to the F52 row's L.B7.1 sweep scope. **Residual, named:** the suite's own ADP-driven seats (7 placeholders + the demoted round-2 resolve) now draw live shared-pool rows — including co-scheduled suites' fixtures — into NO ACTION player FKs until the finally releases them; the same cross-suite class every integer-band db suite already carries; the sweep owns the durable fix.

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (M3 batch 6 — L.C1.5, FINAL fix round)

**Nine findings on PR #159: R375-R377 from the stack-owning reviewer's verification pass, R378-R383 from four independent static lenses that read the diff only. VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER-class, four should-fix, four nits.** Merge target `main` @ 4930bd8; `git merge-tree` clean. **The framing that matters: every pin involved passed. The lenses found what a live verification structurally could not, and three of the six are further doors into the same D160(8) insolvent/stuck-clock state R367 was filed for — R378 being R367's exact species recurring INSIDE R367's own fix. That is four consecutive rounds in which a correction re-introduced its own defect class.**

- **R378 · BLOCKER-class · the E28 arm-3 gate reproduced ONE of the award's TWO refusals, and at a settings-legal `auction_min_bid = 0` the arithmetic that masked the missing one disappears — TAKEN, fixed in the helper.** §3b's header promised "THE COMPARISON IS THE AWARD'S, RE-ASKED AFTER THE WRITE" and implemented it as the single test `v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`. `draft_tick`'s award arm asks **two** things: `open_slots < 1` (E27, `087:3479`) and `price > max_bid` (`087:3484`), and every other consumer pairs them (`draft_force_pick 087:2168-2173`, `draft_nominate 085:478`) because 084:349's `CASE WHEN v_open <= 0 THEN 0` makes a complete roster's `max_bid` a **semantic** zero — at which point `high_bid <= max_bid` is no longer the affordability question. At `min_bid >= 1` the gap is masked (`high_bid >= min_bid >= 1 > 0`, so the money arm raises anyway, with a message about dollars); at **`auction_min_bid = 0`, which is legal** (`league-settings.ts:220` = `min(0)`; 084:210 names the $0 league), both nomination writers open AT min_bid, so an unraised nomination stands at $0 and the gate computed `0 <= 0` and RETURNED. `draft_auction_solvent`'s floor there is `remaining >= 0`. **Driven:** budget $200 / min_bid $0 / total_rounds 2, t2 the standing high bidder at $0 with one pick; `draft_move_player(..., t2, null, 50)` filled its last slot, committed, and every tick then raised E27 into `auction_failures` forever. **Fix:** the gate re-derives `open_slots` alongside `max_bid`, its pass condition is `v_open >= 1 AND v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`, and the capacity case gets **its own sentence** (folding it into the max-bid message prints "$0 max bid" and sends the commissioner after money instead of a roster slot). **The coverage gap was the fixture, not the pin:** new **§I(c)** on a min_bid-$0 world (LM), one unit of `open_slots` either side, plus a min_bid-$1 pin proving the arm is the award's first question rather than a $0 special case. **Probe 7 → 5 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R379 · should-fix · `draft_reset` left the previous run's `draft_bids` live at sequence numbers the restart re-issues, so `draft_undo`'s auction on-clock recovery could seat the WRONG franchise — TAKEN, both halves.** `nomination_seq` IS `current_pick_number`; `draft_reset` rewinds it to 1 (`087:2573`) and `draft_start_internal` re-issues from there (`084:692`/`084:697`), while the recovery lookup (`087:1423`) had **no run discriminator at all** — no `voided_at` filter (deliberately: it must read rows the undo just voided) and no time bound. Two runs' nominations therefore collide on one sequence number, and since the seq→nominator map is not positional (§8.6.7(c) skips complete rosters) the earliest row names a DIFFERENT franchise. **Fix (a):** `draft_reset` stamps its run's rows `voided_at` — rows KEPT, §12.5 stays append-only, the same posture as the `draft_picks` soft-undo beside it — and reset is added as situation **(c)** in the D162 enumeration at `087:230-250` (whose lead-in said "exactly two situations" and now says three), in the spec (**v2.12.4**) and in `voided_at`'s writer inventory, which had said "written ONLY by two sites". **Fix (b):** the lookup scopes to `b.created_at >= v_draft.started_at`, the one discriminator available to a reader that must see voided rows, with a LOUD refusal when `started_at` is NULL on a live/paused draft rather than a silently widened window. Pinned both ways in §K, including the unscoped measurement that shows the ambiguity is real. **Probes 8 and 9 → 1 of 199 RED each**, reverted.
- **R380 · should-fix · `draft_reassign_pick`'s exclusivity check was blind to the one player who must not be assigned: the one under nomination — TAKEN.** On an auction the nominated player has **no** `draft_picks` row until the award writes it (`087:3497`), so a sweep of `draft_picks` passes for exactly him; nothing else on the path reads `current_nomination` (the E28 arms are about money; the §3b gate returns silently when the receiving team is not the high bidder). The award's INSERT then hits `uniq_draft_player_live` (065:178), ARM 2.6's `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` (`087:3581`) swallows it into `auction_failures`, and the nomination never clears — the same stuck clock, reached through the board instead of through the money. `draft_move_player` cannot reach it (it requires a live pick), which is why the guard lives on reassign and only there. Refusal points at `draft_cancel_nomination` — the verb this task shipped. **Probe 10 → 3 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R381 · should-fix · the no-drift pin whose entire job is preventing R367 from recurring was satisfied by a COMMENT — TAKEN, and the weakness was measured rather than argued.** `pg_proc.prosrc` is raw body text INCLUDING comments; `draft_adjust_budget` names the arm-3 helper twice (the R367 comment at `087:776` and the `PERFORM` at `087:781`), so deleting the call and keeping the comment left the pin GREEN. **Proof, not assertion: probe 1 was re-run with exactly that mutation and the pre-R381 predicate still evaluated `TRUE`.** All three sibling pins (`036:230/238/244`) now match the CALL FORM as each helper is actually called (`PERFORM public.X(` for the two gates, `:= public.X(` for the void helper, which returns a count) and assert **cardinality** (`count(*) = N`), because `bool_and` over a shrunken set also returns TRUE. Probe 1's red set consequently GREW by exactly pin 13 — **3 of 181 → 4 of 199** — which is the finding, measured.
- **R375 · should-fix · the stated justification for the eleven-verb mock sweep was false — TAKEN (the sweep KEPT, the reason replaced).** The 087 banner and 036 §M both said "025 already pins their mock refusal" is a claim about function bodies that no longer exist. **It is not:** `025_mock_draft_mode.sql:765-782` pins the mock refusal of `draft_set_clock`/`draft_reassign_pick`/`draft_move_player`, `supabase test db` runs 025 against the fully migrated 001-087 chain, and 025 calls them positionally with fewer arguments — resolving to the new arities through the defaults. Those pins exercise the **post-087 bodies**. The true reason for the sweep is CO-LOCATION: three of the seven were DROP+CREATEd here, so 036 pins the eleven in the post-087 world BESIDE 025's rather than instead of them. **Third instance in this PR of a justification outrunning the facts** — v2.12.3 says exactly why that is dangerous.
- **R382 · nit · pin 127's description inverted the causality — TAKEN (description only; the pin and its arithmetic were right).** It said a cross-team move is refused "because the SLOT it consumes is what shrinks the max bid". From 084:349-350 consuming a slot **raises** max_bid by one min_bid: t2 goes 151/2/150 → 149/1/149, where the $2 price costs $2 and the slot rebates $1, net −$1. The section's own setup comment stated it correctly. Reworded to the measured cause — t2 sits at exact equality after the $49 correction, so any net reduction refuses.
- **R383 · nit · the §M zero-side-effect pin said "measured rather than inferred", and for ten of the eleven verbs it was inferred — TAKEN by WIDENING, not by narrowing the claim.** The counter summed `draft_picks` + `draft_bids` for the mock, and on that fixture only `draft_force_pick` could have added a row to either; every other verb writes where the counter did not look — `leagues.status`/`drafts.status` (reset, end), `drafts.config` (set_clock), `drafts.nomination_order` (set_order), `drafts.budget_adjustments` (adjust_budget), `league_chat` (all). Pointedly, pin 194 one line earlier singles out `draft_reset` as the one whose bypass is an outright §8.8 breach *because it writes leagues.status* — the exact column the composite did not read. Now a 025-§F-style capture of the WHOLE drafts row and the WHOLE leagues row (so `updated_at` alone falsifies a smuggled UPDATE) plus pick/bid/chat/liveness counts. **Probe 11 → 2 of 199 RED; the pre-R383 composite re-run under the identical mutation turned 1** — it watched a mock whose league and draft rows had just been rewritten and reported zero side effects.
- **R376 · nit · the one-off `draft-board-autopick-db.test.ts` red filed as ledger row F70 — TAKEN.** The "re-run without an intervening reset" explanation does not hold: that file carries an error-checked throwing `cleanup()` in both `beforeAll` (`:170`) and `afterAll` (`:224-225`, `:302-305`), hardened after this lane burned on it twice (R285, R286, the F53 class). NOT reproduced this cycle; routed with the F56 shape (observed output, "not reproduced", what to capture next time before re-running).
- **R377 · nit · PROGRESS's spec pointer still read "v2.9.1 (LAW)" — TAKEN.** Stale on `main` identically, so not introduced here, but this PR moves the spec to v2.12.4 and shipping without touching it would leave the pointer more wrong than it found it. Now v2.12.4 with the intervening versions listed.

New **§I(b)** on a new world (LH) that has one, with the one-unit-short pair on both verbs and the same-team arm. **Probe 6 → 10 of 181 RED**, reverted. Migration comment at the gate and the section-11 banner corrected — both claimed the door was already closed.

It also raised and then voided an overload hazard: `CREATE OR REPLACE` with trailing DEFAULT args REPLACED the 3-arg function on a stale DB rather than overloading it (`pg_proc` count 2, and 034 pins that count). **R331's record-arm reasoning was tested rather than read and upheld on all three rejections** — narrowing the replay lookup would re-open 23505 (the same argument that declined the `unique_violation` wrapper — the two positions are consistent, and the unqualified lookup is *why* no wrapper is owed); argument-consistency would redden both shipped E2 pins (the bid replay sends amount 999 and asserts 6; the nominate replay sends a different player); and position inference breaks under D143's cancel-and-renominate, false-refusing a legitimate reconnect retry. - **R330 · should-fix · THE HEADLINE — `draft_place_bid` took only an amount, so a bid in flight across a nomination boundary was applied to whatever player was live when it executed — TAKEN, fixed IN THE RPC (optional identity args + both arms pinned + its own probe)** — the insert took `player_id` from `current_nomination` and `nomination_seq` from `current_pick_number`, both read fresh under the lock, so the RPC could not know what the caller was looking at and E2 did not help (a first-time submit carries a fresh action_id). If nobody raises, 086 awards that player at that price; a manager becomes high bidder on a player they never saw. The snake analogue cannot mis-target because `draft_make_pick` carries `player_id`. §5's sketch prints the amount-only signature, but the same paragraph says "Builder finalizes exact fields" — LATITUDE, not a constraint — and no residual was recorded anywhere (085 banner, the D-entry — then `D147`, renumbered to `D157` by R328 in this same cycle — and the PR body, all three silent). **Resolved (orchestrator decision: fix now in the RPC, do not defer to L.C2.1 — the RPC is the server-authoritative boundary, a route guard would leave the sim, the tests and every future caller exposed, and L.C1.4's completion path awards on this data):** `draft_place_bid` now takes `p_nomination_seq INTEGER DEFAULT NULL` and `p_player_id TEXT DEFAULT NULL` and refuses a mismatch with §16.3's "just went off the board" copy family, checked the moment the live nomination is known and BEFORE the franchise/self-raise/raise/max-bid clauses so a stale bid gets the true reason. **Both arguments, because neither subsumes the other:** `player_id` catches the ordinary moved-on case; `nomination_seq` catches the two states where the SAME player is live under a DIFFERENT nomination — D143's cancel-and-renominate (the sequence number is not consumed) and an undone award returning a player to the pool at a later sequence. **All three arms pinned** (034 §F, pins 43/44/45/46): matching accepted, player-mismatch refused, seq-mismatch refused, and omitted-both unchanged — which is every other bid call in the file and in the wire suite. - **R329 · should-fix · the anti-snipe-disabled pin could not detect the mutation it advertised, and the branch's stated rationale was arithmetically FALSE — TAKEN (reworded everywhere + the discriminating pin ADDED + the silent counterpart recorded)** — the reviewer replaced `085:611–616` with an unconditional `GREATEST(current_deadline, now() + make_interval(secs => v_anti_snipe))` and **all 84 pins and all 3 wire cases stayed GREEN**; found independently by two lenses. The reviewer's better rationale is adopted: the zero branch is also what refuses to INVENT a deadline from NULL. And the previously **unpinned, unrecorded** counterpart now has both — pin 62: at anti_snipe 10 a bid landing after the clock read zero receives a FULL FRESH WINDOW (`now() + 10s`). Defensible under D128's letter and consistent with snake's tick-is-the-enforcer posture, but recorded deliberately rather than left as emergent behavior.

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (DR batch 1)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #157 — DR.1, the full-screen draft-room route, `main...feat/DR.1-fullscreen-route`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER (a real regression on two surfaces), two should-fixes, three nits; ALL SIX TAKEN plus both lane-level recommendations; resolution on the SAME branch per house precedent.** *(The reviewer's own framing, and it is the durable output of this batch: **every claim in the PR that had been MEASURED held up** — the route-manifest diff, the same-cookie middleware differential in both directions, F66 measured on production builds both ways, the D147–D156 verbatim transcription, the shell-provider enumeration surviving an independent 98-file transitive closure. **Every claim that failed was one species: an assertion about the post-change world inferred from the INTENT of the change rather than observed**, written in the *proved* register beside claims that genuinely were proved. Each was one `grep`, one `wc -l`, or one DOM inventory from being caught. That pattern is now **tasks-DR §4.9**, a standing rule for the lane, and **DR.8's item 5 is extended to re-check disclosure PARAGRAPHS, not only F-rows** — three disclosures were wrong here and not one of them was an F-row.)*

- **R340 · BLOCKER · the route-group split REGRESSED a working exit on two surfaces, and every disclosure site asserted the opposite — TAKEN (both components fixed, six sites pinned, measured before and after).** Mechanism: on `main`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx` returned `<AppShell>`, which renders `<AppHeader />` inside `hidden lg:block`; `AppHeader` reads `useHeaderStore`, which `PageHeader` writes. Both components are byte-identical on `main` and this branch — so the lobby's and the launcher's *Back to league* **did render at ≥`lg` on `main` and render nowhere on this branch**. DR.1 did not create the mobile hole (tasks-DR §1 already named it); it widened a below-`lg` defect into an all-widths one, on the two surfaces nobody enumerated. **Reproduced independently before fixing** (dev-local :3123, a purpose-built SCHEDULED league where the dev-auth user is a plain manager, so `isCommish` is false): the lobby inventoried **one link, pointing DEEPER** — `…/draft?practice=1 :: Practice this draft` — and **zero buttons**; the launcher's past-pre-draft arm inventoried **zero links, zero buttons**; its pre-draft arm inventoried **zero links** and four controls that all go further in. The contradicted claim, verbatim (tasks-DR §1, repeated in D159(5) and the PR body): *"the lobby keeps Draft setup / Practice this draft, so no state is a dead end in the meantime"* — but **Draft setup is inside `{isCommish && …}`**, so a plain member never sees it. **Resolved:** `draft-lobby.tsx` gains an in-card *Back to league* **outside** the commissioner gate; `mock-draft-launcher.tsx` gains one at container level, **above the `preDraft` fork**, so both arms and every `MockList` state keep it. Not deferred to DR.2, per the finding. **Re-measured after the fix, same URLs:** lobby → **2 links** (`…/leagues/<id> :: Back to league` + the practice CTA), launcher pre-draft arm → **1 link** (the exit), launcher past-pre-draft arm → **1 link** (the exit) where it had none. New pin file **`src/components/draft/room-exits.test.ts` (5 pins)**, written to survive DR.2: every assertion runs against the source with **`<PageHeader …/>` elements deleted**, so a header can never satisfy them and they stay green when DR.2 removes those calls. **Four probes shown and reverted** — delete the lobby exit → 2/5 RED (both lobby pins); move it back inside `{isCommish && …}` → **exactly 1/5 RED** (the gate pin alone, proving it discriminates placement, not presence); delete the launcher exit → 2/5 RED; move it inside the `preDraft` arm only → **exactly 1/5 RED** (the both-arms pin). The correction is written at all three disclosure sites (tasks-DR §1, D159(5), the room docblock) and **the live room is now named as the one remaining exit-less state**, which is DR.2's Exit Draft to close.
- **R339 · should-fix · the C46 rename note claimed line numbers "still land" when every one was off by +22 — TAKEN (renumbered, and the offset proven wholesale).** The claim: *"the file is still 1013 lines … every `snake-draft-room.tsx:NNN` citation still lands (re-verified)"*. True of the `git mv`; false of the commit, which added a 22-line docblock above every landmark. Verified: `main` 1013 → branch 1035; `:389`→411, `:443`→465, `:450`→472, `:666`→688, `:719`→741, `:768`→790, and §1's `PageHeader` list `:666/:169/:250/:949/:969/:1001` was really 688/191/272/971/991/1023. **Six task banners (DR.2–DR.7) navigate by these numbers.** **Resolved:** after this cycle's own docblock corrections the file is **1052 lines** and the offset is **+39**; **tasks-DR §1 and the DR.2–DR.7 banners are renumbered** with each anchor also named by symbol (§4.9's preference — a symbol survives the next edit), and §3's D-entries / §6's dispositions are deliberately left at their as-authored numbers because §4 here quotes D147–D156 verbatim (both the note and the room docblock say "add 39" for those). The offset is established rather than spot-checked: **`main:snake-draft-room.tsx` line *N* is byte-identical to `draft-room.tsx` line *N+39* for every *N* in 101–1013**, the single exception being the renamed `export function` line — and every renumbered anchor was re-read by content afterwards.
- **R341 · should-fix · `(shell)/not-found.tsx`'s docblock was rewritten FOR accuracy and still opened with a false sentence — TAKEN, and the measurement turned out to be bigger than either side had it.** The sentence: *"Renders inside the app shell, so the nav survives and the user is never stranded."* **Measured on production builds, signed in, both revisions** — and the two halves disagree, which is why the claim survived so long: **server-rendered HTML has NO shell** (`/app/nfl/ZZZ` → 404, branch 17,621 bytes / `main` @ 9c81f7c 17,109 bytes, `pr-rail-strip` ×0, `h-header` ×0, no sidebar links; control `/app/lists` on the same session → 200, 44,187 bytes, `pr-rail-strip` ×1, `h-header` ×2, sidebar "Home" ×2), while **after hydration the shell IS there** (same URL, fresh `navigate`: DOM 34,450 bytes branch / 33,938 `main`, `pr-rail-strip` ×1, two sidebar "Home" links). So the nav does survive — but the **first paint of any `/app` 404 is chrome-less, and stays that way if JS fails**, which makes the page's own *Back to home* button the only exit the server actually sends.
